info.title: Exclaimer Cloud API
info.description:
Introduction

The Exclaimer Cloud API is designed to offer partners the ability to provision and manage Exclaimer Cloud tenants. The endpoints are as follows:

  • Development:
    • https://sandbox-cloudapi.exclaimer.com
  • Live:
    • https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com

The URL required to call the API is made up of three parts:

[endpoint]/[version]/[resource-or-action]

In addition to the URL you must use the correct HTTP method, GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, etc.

e.g. To add a new subscription
Method: POST
Endpoint URL: https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/exclaimerapi
Version: 1.0
Resource: subscriptions

This results in:
POST https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/exclaimerapi/1.0/subscriptions

e.g. To determine how many mailboxes are associated with the subscription
Method: GET
Endpoint URL: https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/exclaimerapi
Version: 1.0
Resource: subscriptions/{SubscriptionID}/mailbox-count

{SubscriptionID} represents a placeholder where you provide the subscription you are interested in

This would results in:
GET https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/exclaimerapi/1.0/subscriptions/sub123/mailbox-count

You may also be provided with a custom endpoint such as "yourcompany". In this case the above example URLs would look like this:

https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/yourcompany/1.0/subscriptions
https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/yourcompany/1.0/subscriptions/sub123/mailbox-count

Although the examples in the API Reference section of this document start with "exclaimerapi", just remember to use the URL provided.

Usage

All calls to the Exclaimer Cloud API must include a header called ExAPIToken with a value that will be provided to you separately. This will allow the API to identify you. Any calls to the API without this token will result in a 401 Unauthorized error.

Issues with the service

If any issues arise when using with the service, such as an invalid request or a server problem, you will be notified via standard HTTP status codes, as documented below and against each API.

400 Missing Field

This can occur when required fields have either not been supplied, or have been supplied but are empty.

A json structure will be returned detailing the missing fields.

400 Bad Request

This can occur when the provided values do not meet the expected format. e.g., The value contains too many characters, or is supplied as a string when a number is expected.

A json structure will be returned detailing the error.

401 Unauthorized

This can occur when either the API token is not supplied, or is invalid.

403 Forbidden

This can occur if the caller of the API has provided a valid token, but does not have the required permissions to perform the action.

This can also occur if the caller of the API owns a resource and attempts an action that would leave the resource in a problem state. e.g. trying to delete the owner of a subscription.

404 Not Found

This can occur when the URL does not match a valid API signature, or when a parameter is specified with a resource that does not exist, for example you supplied a subscription ID that we have no record of.

415 Unsupported Media Type

This can occur if the HTTP Content-Type header contains a media type that is not supported by the API.

Please specify application/json.

500 Internal Server Error

This indicates that an unexpected error has occurred.

Please let Exclaimer support know about these issues.

Casing

The Exclaimer Cloud API uses Pascal case JSON, i.e. a capital letter at the beginning of each word, and abbreviations. e.g. SubscriptionID, NumberOfNFRUsers. Another popular convention is to use camel case, i.e. the first word using a lower case letter followed by a capital letter for each subsequent word. e.g. subscriptionId, numberOfNfrUsers. To cater for both of these conventions, Exclaimer Cloud API will accept JSON in either format.

{ "SubscriptionID": "sub-1", CountryCode: "GB" }
... is treated as equivalent to ...
{ "subscriptionId": "sub-1", countryCode: "GB" }

This also applies to query string parameters.

/subscriptions?ContinuationToken=262145
... is treated as equivalent to ...
/subscriptions?continuationToken=262145

N.B. This does not apply to path parameters or JSON values, which may be treated in a case sensitive manner.

Responses are always return in Pascal case.

Paging of results

Some requests can potentially return a large number of items.In this case the results are automatically paged, and only a subset of the results will be returned. You can specify which page you want and how many items the page should contain.If no paging details are specified in the request, then the first 50 items will be returned.

The response will contain paging information allowing you manually calculate how to page through all items.

Alternatively, you can use the simplified ContinuationToken. When this is returned, you can simply provide it in the next request, and the next page of results will be returned, based on the same page size. When there are no more pages, ContinuationToken will no longer be returned*. You can also provide a ContinuationToken value of 0 to get the first page using defaults. This way you never need to think about paging at all. i.e. Make a call with ContinuationToken set to 0, then keep calling with the ContinuationToken returned until ContinuationToken is no longer present*.

If both the ContinuationToken and Page/PageSize values are specified, then ContinuationToken takes precedence and Page/PageSize will be ignored.

* The property will not be returned in the results, so depending on your programming language, this may appear as null, or undefined.

Deprecated features and APIs

From time-to-time the Exclaimer Cloud API needs to change to reflect features that are no longer available, or that have been replaced with alternative features that offer added value. For compatibility, we make every effort to ensure that existing consumers can continue to use both the old and new features until all subscriptions have been migrated.

When this type of change is made, existing consumers can continue to use the API as normal, but we encourage you to take advantage of the new features as soon as practical. New consumers will only have access to the new features, and will not be able to access the deprecated features or associated APIs. In such cases, if you try to use deprecated functionality, you will receive a 400 Bad Request, or a 404 Not Found, depending on the scenario.

These changes will be marked with a deprecated indicator and an explanation:

API/PropertyDate of change
Details of the deprecated feature, API, or property.

By default, deprecated APIs, properties, and examples, are not shown. To view them, click the "Show deprecated features" checkbox at the top-right of the page. This can also be done via a query parameter so you can bookmark the page with this on by default.

e.g. https://cloudapi.exclaimer.com/?showDeprecatedFeatures=true

Issues with the documentation

If you discover any errors within this document, please let Exclaimer know. We make every effort to keep the document accurate and up-to-date.

post.description:
2025-02-17
This endpoint is deprecated. Please use the V2 endpoint at /v2.0/subscriptions instead, which provides enhanced support for marketplace scenarios and SKU-based product specification.

This request will create a new subscription and adds it to the Exclaimer Cloud service.

A new user will be created for the email address provided if one doesn't already exist.

If you pass a SubscriptionID and UserID, these values will be used when creating the subscription, otherwise they'll be randomly generated and returned to you. You will need the subscription ID for other operations, such as updating the mailbox count, or ending the subscription.

get.description:
This request will return details of each of your subscriptions held in the Exclaimer Cloud service.
You can apply filters:
  • to only return active subscriptions, otherwise all subscriptions, including inactive ones, will be returned.
  • to only return subscriptions associated with a specific reseller.
If no subscriptions match the filter, an empty array will be returned.

parameters.name: Page
parameters.description:
Page numbers start at 1.

See the section "Paging of results" at the beginning of the document.
Results are ordered by the date the subscription was added.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description:
Defaults to 50. Maximum 200.

See the section "Paging of results" at the beginning of the document.

parameters.name: ContinuationToken
parameters.description: A token that can be used to get the next page of results without supplying paging values.

parameters.name: ActiveOnly
parameters.description:
When true, returns only subscriptions with an Active status. When false, returns all subscriptions irrespective of status*.

*When used in conjunction with OverageOnly this will return only active subscriptions that have an overage.

parameters.name: OverageOnly
parameters.description:
When true, returns only subscriptions with an overage. When false, returns all subscriptions irrespective of whether there is overage or not*.

*When used in conjunction with ActiveOnly this will return only active subscriptions that have an overage.

parameters.name: ResellerID
parameters.description: When provided, returns only subscriptions for this reseller. When not provided, returns all subscriptions irrespective of reseller.

post.description:
This request will create a new subscription using Version 2 of the API, which introduces SKU-based product specification and enhanced support for marketplace scenarios.

V2 changes include:

  • SKU is now required and determines the product, tier, and NFR status
  • EndUser is required and includes a Domain field
  • Reseller includes a Domain field (required for non-Marketplace subscriptions)
  • BillingGroup is a new optional field for grouping subscriptions
  • SubscriptionProductCode, Tier, NFR, and NumberOfNFRUsers fields are deprecated and should not be used

A new user will be created for the email address provided if one doesn't already exist.

If you pass a SubscriptionID and UserID, these values will be used when creating the subscription, otherwise they'll be randomly generated and returned to you. You will need the subscription ID for other operations, such as updating the mailbox count, or ending the subscription.

Currency Immutability: Once a subscription is created, the currency cannot be changed.

Marketplace Behavior: For Marketplace subscriptions, the system will auto-populate EndUser fields from the email address if not explicitly provided. The Reseller field is optional for Marketplace subscriptions.

This request allows you to add new users to a subscription.

The same user can be added to multiple subscriptions.

Note that you cannot modify an existing subscription user with this API. However, if the user has previously been deleted, they can be re-added.

put.description:
This request allows you to cancel a subscription transfer that you've previously issued a transfer request for.

Once the transfer request is cancelled, the subscription will no longer show as pending transfer. If someone tries to claim the subscription, their request will be rejected.

parameters.name: SubscriptionID
parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription to cancel. This is the same ID you specified when issuing the transfer request.

post.description:
This request allows you to claim a subscription that's currently owned by someone else.

You can optionally specify additional details for the subscription, such as providing a meaningful ID, or associating it with one of your existing resellers, and/or end users.

This is the second half or a two part transfer handshake. See Initiate Subscription Transfer for the first half of the process.

In order to claim a subscription you must first have a valid token that can be used in the transfer process. This token will be provided either by the current subscription owner, or by Exclaimer. Once the token has been used, it will be invalidated, and cannot be reused.

Self claiming: It's possible to claim a subscription that you've previously issued a transfer request for, right up until the point at which the subscription has been claimed by someone else. While we would recommend you use the Cancel Subscription Transfer API instead, if you do use this we recommend only specifying the TransferToken and no other details. In this case, all existing subscription details, including Subscription ID, Reseller, and End User, will remain unchanged.

get.description: This request will return a list of data centers along with which ones can be used with Office 365, and which can be used with GSuite. If a data center is not available for a provider, then the corresponding field will not be returned.

put.description:
This request will deactivate a subscription.

The service will no longer stamp emails for this subscription and the end user will no longer be able to load the template editor, however we will not block the users email. This endpoint should be used if you intend to reactivate the subscription in the near future.

parameters.name: SubscriptionID
parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription. This is the same ID you specified, or was automatically generated, when the subscription was created, i.e., when calling Add Subscription.

delete.description:
This request allows you to remove a user from a subscription.

Note that this only removes the user from the specified subscription. If they have also been added to other subscriptions, those will remain unaffected.

You cannot remove the subscription owner, added during Add Subscription. You will receive a 403 Forbidden if you try.

If you wish to re-add a deleted user, just call Add Subscription User again.

parameters.name: SubscriptionID
parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription. This is the same ID you specified, or was automatically generated, when the subscription was created, i.e., when calling Add Subscription.

parameters.name: UserID
parameters.description:
This can either be your reference for the user, or the user's email address.
Both of these are the same as the ID you specified, or was automatically generated, or the email address used, when the subscription was created i.e., when calling Add Subscription, or when adding a user through Add Subscription User.

get.description:
This request returns a list of all users across all of your subscriptions.

An entry is returned for each unique user along with details of which subscriptions they have access to, and the roles they're assigned within those subscriptions.

The same user, determined by email address, can have a different UserID within each subscription.

parameters.name: Page
parameters.description:
Page numbers start at 1.

See the section "Paging of results" at the beginning of the document.
Results are ordered by the date the subscription was added.

parameters.name: PageSize
parameters.description:
Defaults to 50. Maximum 200.

See the section "Paging of results" at the beginning of the document.

parameters.name: ContinuationToken
parameters.description: A token that can be used to get the next page of results without supplying paging values.

put.description:
This request will end a subscription.

When a subscription is ended it becomes dormant and emails will no longer be processed via the Exclaimer Cloud service. The user's email needs to be redirected so it no longer gets sent through our system before calling this endpoint.

When actioned, the subscription is ended immediately, and the subscription will no longer appear in the Exclaimer Customer Portal.

parameters.name: SubscriptionID
parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription. This is the same ID you specified, or was automatically generated, when the subscription was created, i.e., when calling Add Subscription.

get.description:
This request returns the current usage against the ApiUser's mailbox allocation.

Note: This end-point is only available to Managed Service Providers on the Elite program.

post.description:
This request initiates a subscription transfer.

This is the first half or a two part transfer handshake. See Claim Subscription Transfer for the second half of the process.

This requests puts the target subscription into a state of transfer until it gets claimed. The request returns a Transfer Token that may be used by another consumer to take ownership of the subscription.

parameters.name: SubscriptionID
parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription. This is the same ID you specified, or was automatically generated, when the subscription was created, i.e., when calling Add Subscription.

put.description:
This request allows you to specify that the subscription is not for resale.

A subscription can be changed from being not for resale to a standard subscription, and vise versa, at any time.

N.B. This feature is only available to consumers that support NFR licenses.

post.description:
This request will assign a different user to be the owner of a subscription.

The new owner must already exist against the subscription, and must have the Admin role.

If you want to change the owner to a new subscription user, you can use the Add Subscription User API to create that user first.

If the existing subscription user does not have the Admin role, you can use the Update Subscription User Roles API to give them that role.

If you wish to delete the original owner, you can use the Delete Subscription User API after this request.

parameters.description: Your reference for the subscription. This is the same ID you specified, or was automatically generated, when the subscription was created, i.e., when calling Add Subscription.

N.B. You cannot change from an Office365 subscription to a GSuite subscription, or vise versa.

post.description:
Creates a new subscription for Managed Service Provider (MSP) API users.

This endpoint is only available to API users with MSP (Managed Service Provider) access.

If you provide a SubscriptionID, it must be unique for your API user account. You will need this ID for subsequent operations such as updating the subscription or ending it.

The EndUser and Reseller objects are optional. If provided, all fields within them become required. These allow you to associate the subscription with your own end user and reseller references.

The data center where the subscription will be created.

EU - Europe
UK - UK
US - US

A code representing the type of product being requested. Defaults to EXCL-M-PRO if not specified.

MSP accounts are limited to PRO tier subscriptions. Available SKUs:

EXCL-G-PRO - Exclaimer Pro for Google Workspace

ClaimSubscriptionTransfer.description:
This request allows you to claim a subscription that's currently owned by someone else.

You can optionally specify additional details for the subscription, such as providing a meaningful ID, or associating it with one of your existing resellers, and/or end users.

This is the second half or a two part transfer handshake. See Initiate Subscription Transfer for the first half of the process.

In order to claim a subscription you must first have a valid token that can be used in the transfer process. This token will be provided either by the current subscription owner, or by Exclaimer. Once the token has been used, it will be invalidated, and cannot be reused.

Self claiming: It's possible to claim a subscription that you've previously issued a transfer request for, right up until the point at which the subscription has been claimed by someone else. While we would recommend you use the Cancel Subscription Transfer API instead, if you do use this we recommend only specifying the TransferToken and no other details. In this case, all existing subscription details, including Subscription ID, Reseller, and End User, will remain unchanged.

NumberOfNFRUsers.description:
Specifies the number of users allocated as not for resale.
N.B. When the SKU includes NRF, this value is required; providing this value when NFR is not included will result in an error.

UpdateSubscriptionSKU.description:
This request allows you to use a code to change specific aspects of an existing subscription.

N.B. You cannot change from an Office365 subscription to a GSuite subscription, or vise versa.

UpdateSubscriptionTier.title: UpdateSubscriptionTierRequest

Tier.description:
The tier you want to change to. 2023-04-03
The ExclaimerCloud and SignatureMarketingSuite tiers have been replaced by ExclaimerStarter, ExclaimerStandard, and ExclaimerPro. For compatibility, existing consumers can continue to use the original tiers, along with the new tiers. New consumers can only use the new tiers.

ExclaimerStarter
ExclaimerStandard

Note: Managed-Service-Provider accounts are limited to only creating ExclaimerPro tier subscriptions.

UpdateSubscriptionTier.description: This request allows you to change the subscription tier.

UpdateSubscriptionUserRoles.title: UpdateSubscriptionUserRolesRequest

Roles.description:
The roles you wish to user to have. The user must be assigned a role, but can have one or both.

Admin - Has full control over signatures and settings
Editor - Can create/edit and re-order signatures for permitted folders

Roles are not case-sensitive.

UpdateSubscriptionUserRoles.description:
This request allows you to modify the roles of an existing subscription user.

Note that the subscription owner, added during Add Subscription, must have the Admin role. You will receive a 403 Forbidden if you try to remove it.
